title: Factorization of the affine pushforward homology comparison
statement: Let D and B be commutative rings, psi:B→D, Cg any unbounded complex of D-modules, i an integer, and assume the derived category of sheaves of modules on every scheme exists. Let T be affine tilde over B, F restriction along psi, and sigma the canonical ordinary affine pushforward comparison. With the zero-map preservation instance for tilde over D followed by ordinary pushforward, the explicit affineTildePushforwardCohomologyMap [lem-pc-affine-tilde-pushforward-cohomology-normalization] equals T applied to the inverse restriction homology comparison, followed by the inverse tilde homology comparison on the short complex of the termwise restriction of Cg, followed by the inverse quotient/homology comparison at the termwise tilde of the termwise restriction of Cg, homology of Q applied to the termwise sigma comparison, and homology of the actual right-derived unit. No tensor model, module derived counit or coefficient complex map occurs. More generally, composing the displayed expanded factors with tilde of any B-module morphism v:S→res_psi(H^i(Cg)), and combining its first map with the inverse restriction comparison, equals tilde(v) followed by the normalized cohomology map.

proof.text: Expand the defining pushforward cohomology map. Its initial factor is the inverse homology comparison for restriction followed by exact tilde. Use the existing RingTensorCohomology.mapHomologyIso_hom_comp API of MixedTensorUnderlyingHomology. Cancel the composite forward comparison and the two inverse/forward pairs to obtain the inverse composite comparison. Apply it to Cg.sc i.

Compose this equality with the quotient/homology comparison, homology of the termwise ordinary pushforward comparison, and homology of the right-derived unit. Use the equality between the inverse of a natural-isomorphism component and the component of its inverse. The remaining factors are precisely those in the defining formula. All constructions are valid for zero complexes and zero rings. Compose on the left with tilde(v) and use functoriality.

lean.statement:
theorem affineTildePushforwardHomologyFactorization
    (D B : Type u) [CommRing D] [CommRing B] (ψ : B →+* D)
    [(affineTildeFunctor D ⋙
      Scheme.Modules.pushforward (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom ψ))).PreservesZeroMorphisms]
    (Cg : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{u} D) ℤ) (i : ℤ)
    (S : ModuleCat.{u} B)
    (v : S ⟶ (ModuleCat.restrictScalars ψ).obj (Cg.homology i)) :
    let T := affineTildeFunctor B
    let _ : T.Additive := instAdditiveModuleCatCarrierModulesSpecOfFunctor
    let _ : T.PreservesHomology := tilde_preservesHomology B
    let H := DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor
      (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings (Spec (.of B)).toRingedSpace)) i
    let σ := affineTildePushforwardComparison D B ψ
    let a := (σ.hom.mapHomologicalComplex
      (.up ℤ)).app Cg
    -- Use the same pushforward functor for the comparison and its derived unit.
    let P : SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings (Spec (.of D)).toRingedSpace) ⥤
        SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings (Spec (.of B)).toRingedSpace) :=
      Scheme.Modules.pushforward (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom ψ))
    let _ : P.Additive := RingedSpace.moduleDirectImage_additive
      (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom ψ)).toLRSHom.toShHom
    let β := P.rightDerivedFunctorUnit.app
      ((HomotopyCategory.quotient _ (.up ℤ)).obj
        (((affineTildeFunctor D).mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ)).obj Cg))
    T.map (v ≫ ((Cg.sc i).mapHomologyIso (ModuleCat.restrictScalars ψ)).inv) ≫
        (((((ModuleCat.restrictScalars ψ).mapHomologicalComplex
          (.up ℤ)).obj Cg).sc i).mapHomologyIso T).inv ≫
        (DerivedCategory.homologyFunctorFactors _ i).inv.app
          ((T.mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ)).obj
            (((ModuleCat.restrictScalars ψ).mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ)).obj Cg)) ≫
        H.map (DerivedCategory.Q.map a) ≫ H.map β =
    T.map v ≫ affineTildePushforwardCohomologyMap D B ψ Cg i
